angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 349,588 km at 82.09 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.1812 +/- 0.0173 mas (same row, RUWE 1.11): 82.09 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.502498 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2453 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 349,588 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.549 (0.509 to 0.589) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3720.23 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2453 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2453 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2453.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.776, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, TOI-2453: main object type Em*, Emission-line Star
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2453 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.41349, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 3295485490907597696, flags_flame 00: age_flame 13.244643 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 7.191202 to 13.5)
